Not clear or exact — Vago/a / impreciso/a.
Hard to see clearly — Borroso/a / difuso/a.
A vague shape moved in the fog.
Raise something to a higher place — Elevar / levantar.
Elevate your leg to reduce the swelling.
Raise in rank or quality — Elevar / ascender.
The win elevated them to first place.
A game where prizes are won by chance — Lotería.
Something decided by luck — Lotería / cuestión de suerte.
Getting a seat is a lottery.
Provide the money for something — Financiar.
v|Adjective: financial. Plural noun: finances, meaning the money you have.
Get something, often with effort — Obtener / conseguir.
He obtained a copy of the report.
A building where films are shown — Cine.
We went to the cinema on Friday.
The art of making films — Cine / séptimo arte.
American English usually says movie theater and the movies.
Something that happens, especially something important — Acontecimiento / suceso.
The wedding was the event of the year.
One item in a sports programme — Prueba / competición.
The final event is the relay.
Phrase: in any event, meaning anyway. Adjective: eventful.
Throw something away because it is not needed — Descartar / desechar.
v|Also used in card games: discard a card.
Fly high in the air — Remontarse / planear.
An eagle soared above the valley.
Rise very quickly — Dispararse / subir vertiginosamente.
v|Careful: soar is to rise, sore means painful.
Coming after something else — Posterior / subsiguiente.
Show a connection between things — Relacionar.
The study relates diet to health.
Understand and feel for someone — Identificarse con.
I can relate to that feeling.
Thank you for your prompt reply.
Make someone do or say something — Impulsar / provocar.
The noise prompted him to look out.
Remind an actor of the words — Apuntar.
Someone prompted her from the wings.
Done too quickly and not carefully — Apresurado/a / precipitado/a.
Noun: haste. Adverb: hastily. Comparative: hastier.
Burn the surface of something — Chamuscar / quemar superficialmente.
She scorched the shirt with the iron.
Dry up with heat — Agostar / resecar.
Literary. Adjective: tempestuous, also used of stormy relationships.
Showing that you understand someone's trouble — Comprensivo/a / solidario/a.
She gave me a sympathetic look.
In favour of an idea — Favorable / afín.
He is sympathetic to the plan.
Noun: sympathy. False friend: simpático in Spanish is nice or friendly, which in English is friendly or likeable.
Make up for something bad — Compensar / redimir.
One good scene redeemed the film.
Exchange a coupon or ticket for something — Canjear.
He redeemed his watch from the pawnshop.
v|Noun: redemption. Phrase: a redeeming feature.
Begin again after a break — Reanudar / retomar.
v|Careful: a résumé with accents is a short account of your career.
Getting on well together — Armonía / concordia.
Musical notes that sound well together — Armonía.
Stop yourself from doing something — Abstenerse de.
The part of a song that is repeated — Estribillo.
v|Pattern: refrain from doing something. Formal.
A drug that dulls pain and causes sleep — Narcótico / estupefaciente.
The doctor gave him a narcotic.
The plant has a narcotic effect.
Often plural in police use: narcotics.
Person who will receive someone's property or title — Heredero/a.
He is the heir to a large fortune.
The h is silent: it sounds like air. Feminine form: heiress. Verb: inherit.
The majestic cathedral filled the square.
Become smaller and smaller — Menguar / ir disminuyendo.
Our savings dwindled month by month.
More than what is needed — Excedente / superávit.
The farm has a surplus of milk.
Person who betrays their country or friends — Traidor(a).
He was shot as a traitor.
She spoke in a deliberate voice.
The jury deliberated for six hours.
v|The adjective ends in a short -at, the verb in -eit. Adverb: deliberately.
Person who damages property on purpose — Vándalo/a.
A long period without rain — Sequía.
Spelling trap: it sounds like out, not like ought.
Accept and obey a rule or decision — Acatar / atenerse a.
You must abide by the referee's decision.
Put up with something — Soportar / aguantar.
v|Pattern: abide by a rule. The second sense is nearly always negative.
Join parts into one whole — Unificar.
The new leader unified the party.
The top of a mountain — Cima / cumbre.
They reached the summit at dawn.
A meeting of world leaders — Cumbre.
Pay careful attention to advice or a warning — Hacer caso de / atender.
He did not heed the warning.
She paid no heed to the sign.
